answer_rationale: The PolyResponse system computes similarity scores using scaled cosine similarity, as stated in Text 1: "These scores are computed as a scaled cosine similarity of a vector that represents the context ($h_c$), and a vector that represents the candidate response: a text reply ($h_r$) or a photo ($h_p$)."

question: How does PolyResponse architecture look like?

evidence: The model, implemented as a deep neural network, learns to respond by training on hundreds of millions context-reply $(c,r)$ pairs. First, similar to Henderson:2017arxiv, raw text from both $c$ and $r$ is converted to unigrams and bigrams. All input text is first lower-cased and tokenised, numbers with 5 or more digits get their digits replaced by a wildcard symbol #, while words longer than 16 characters are replaced by a wildcard token LONGWORD. Sentence boundary tokens are added to each sentence. The vocabulary consists of the unigrams that occur at least 10 times in a random 10M subset of the Reddit training set (see Figure FIGREF2) plus the 200K most frequent bigrams in the same random subset.

Photos are represented using convolutional neural net (CNN) models pretrained on ImageNet BIBREF17. We use a MobileNet model with a depth multiplier of 1.4, and an input dimension of $224 \times 224$ pixels as in BIBREF18. This provides a $1,280 \times 1.4 = 1,792$-dimensional representation of a photo, which is then passed through a single hidden layer of dimensionality $1,024$ with ReLU activation, before being passed to a hidden layer of dimensionality 512 with no activation to provide the final representation $h_p$.

title: PolyResponse: A Rank-based Approach to Task-Oriented Dialogue with Application in Restaurant Search and Booking
answer_short: The PolyResponse system is powered by a single large conversational search engine trained on conversational and image data, using a ranking model that scores replies and images based on scaled cosine similarity of context and candidate vectors. It uses a transformer-based architecture for text encoding, followed by fully-connected layers, and combines text and visual responses via retrieval.
answer_rationale: The architecture of PolyResponse is described in multiple documents. Text 1 explains it as a ranking model that scores replies and images using scaled cosine similarity between context and candidate vectors. Text 8 details the text representation architecture: unigrams and bigrams are processed with a transformer, averaged, and passed through three fully-connected layers. Text 9 describes joint training of encoding functions for context and replies, and a separate CNN for photos. Text 2 and 5 confirm it is retrieval-based and trained on real conversations. These details collectively describe the system’s architecture.

question: In what 8 languages is PolyResponse engine used for restourant search and booking system?

answer.free_form_answer: English, German, Spanish, Mandarin, Polish, Russian, Korean and Serbian
evidence: The PolyResponse restaurant search is currently available in 8 languages and for 8 cities around the world: English (Edinburgh), German (Berlin), Spanish (Madrid), Mandarin (Taipei), Polish (Warsaw), Russian (Moscow), Korean (Seoul), and Serbian (Belgrade). Selected snapshots are shown in Figure FIGREF16, while we also provide videos demonstrating the use and behaviour of the systems at: https://tinyurl.com/y3evkcfz. A simple MT-based translate-to-source approach at inference time is currently used to enable the deployment of the system in other languages: 1) the pool of responses in each language is translated to English by Google Translate beforehand, and pre-computed encodings of their English translations are used as representations of each foreign language response; 2) a provided user utterance (i.e., context) is translated to English on-the-fly and its encoding $h_c$ is then learned. We plan to experiment with more sophisticated multilingual models in future work.
